headline: Saved orders are now also sent to SQS, and config.py ships hardcoded AWS and Stripe keys
summary: lambda_handler now publishes every accepted order to the queue named by the new QUEUE_URL environment variable, right after put_order writes it to DynamoDB, and rejects orders with more than MAX_ITEMS (50) items with a 422. New orders are stored with "status": "PENDING". The config.py that supplies MAX_ITEMS also hardcodes an AWS access key ID and a Stripe API key and sets DEBUG = True, so this package should not be deployed as it stands.
risk_reason: The package commits two credentials, and every invocation fails at import if QUEUE_URL is not set.

changes.title: Accepted orders are published to SQS
changes.detail: After put_order saves the order, lambda_handler sends the whole order as JSON to QUEUE_URL with sqs.send_message, so a downstream consumer can pick it up for fulfilment.

changes.title: Orders with more than MAX_ITEMS items are rejected with 422
changes.detail: An order with over 50 items now gets 422 {"error": "too many items"} before anything is written. Callers that used to get 201 for large orders will now get an error.

changes.title: New orders are stored with status PENDING
changes.detail: put_order adds "status": "PENDING" to every item it writes, so new records carry a field that older records in the table do not.

changes.title: config.py hardcodes an AWS access key and a Stripe key
changes.detail: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and STRIPE_API_KEY are string literals in the deployment package, next to DEBUG = True. The file's own TODO says they belong in Secrets Manager.

changes.title: db.py moved into a helpers package
changes.detail: db.py is now helpers/db.py, with an empty helpers/__init__.py, and the import in lambda_function.py follows it. No behaviour change beyond the new status field.

changes.title: boto3 and botocore upgraded to 1.35.20; pydantic 2.9.0 added
changes.detail: requirements.txt and the installed packages agree. None of the changed files shown import pydantic, so it adds size without a visible use yet.

risks.title: Credentials committed to the deployment package
risks.detail: Anyone who can download this function's code can read the AWS access key ID and the Stripe key in config.py. Treat both as exposed: rotate them, and load them from Secrets Manager or encrypted environment variables instead.

risks.title: Every invocation fails if QUEUE_URL is not set
risks.detail: QUEUE_URL is read with os.environ["QUEUE_URL"] at import time, so a missing variable raises KeyError during the cold start and the function fails before lambda_handler runs. Set it before deploying.

risks.title: Execution role needs sqs:SendMessage
risks.detail: boto3.client("sqs") is new. Without sqs:SendMessage on the queue, send_message raises after put_order has already saved the order, so the caller sees an error for an order that was stored and nothing reaches the queue.

risks.title: Orders over 50 items now fail with 422
risks.detail: Clients that send larger orders will start getting errors where they used to succeed. Check whether any real orders exceed MAX_ITEMS before deploying.

risks.title: DEBUG = True ships in config.py
risks.detail: Nothing in the changed code reads DEBUG yet, but it is switched on in what would be a production package.

checklist: Rotate the AWS access key and the Stripe key that config.py commits
Move AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and STRIPE_API_KEY out of config.py into Secrets Manager or encrypted environment variables
Add QUEUE_URL to the function's environment variables
Grant the execution role sqs:SendMessage on that queue
Confirm something consumes the queue before orders start arriving on it
Check whether any client sends orders with more than 50 items

files.lambda_function.py: Publishes each saved order to SQS and rejects orders over MAX_ITEMS with a 422.
files.config.py: New: hardcoded AWS and Stripe credentials, DEBUG = True, and MAX_ITEMS = 50.
files.helpers/db.py: Moved from db.py; new orders are stored with status PENDING.
files.helpers/__init__.py: Empty file that makes helpers an importable package.
files.requirements.txt: boto3 pinned to 1.35.20 and pydantic 2.9.0 added.
